transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is... I’ve been noticing I’m not following through on things the way I should. It’s not like I don’t care—I really do start them with every intention of finishing.

After audits, or even mentorship events, there are these follow-up items—an email, a review note, a form—and I’ll think I handled it, or I’ll be in the middle of it, and then a few days later I find out the final piece just never actually got done. It’s been embarrassing, honestly. I kept telling myself it was just being busy, but it’s happened enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone.

Thinking back, would you say you've had this kind of trouble finishing tasks and staying organized since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started or gotten noticeably worse recently?

I think it’s been there for a long time, honestly. I don’t want to overstate it, because I did well in school overall, but even in elementary school my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I’d lose assignments or rush past little details. I’d need reminders to actually finish work.

My mom still kind of laughs about it—like, I could do well on a test but forget the project sitting in my backpack. And I was apparently the kid who would talk out of turn sometimes. So… yes, I guess it’s not completely new. It’s just more noticeable now, maybe because the stakes are higher.

Aside from talking out of turn as a kid, do you currently notice things like feeling restless, having trouble sitting still, fidgeting, or feeling like you need to be constantly moving or doing something?

Um… yes, I think so. I don’t know if it looks obvious from the outside, but during a long review, sitting still can feel really uncomfortable. Like there’s this pressure building up inside me, and I start feeling like I need to get up.

I’ll walk to the printer, or get water, or sort of invent a reason to move around. It’s not that I’m trying to avoid the work, exactly… it just gets hard to stay planted in the chair for too long. Does that make sense?
Beyond work, do you notice these same kinds of difficulties—like losing track of tasks, restlessness, or trouble focusing—affecting your home life or relationships as well?

Yes… I mean, I wish I could say it was just at work, but it does show up at home too.

I try not to make it sound worse than it is, because I do care and I’m not trying to be unreliable. But my husband has started taking over some of the bills and commitments that I said I would handle, because… honestly, he can’t always count on me to finish them when I say I will.

And at work it’s gotten more uncomfortable. Some of the missed follow-up and little unfinished pieces have actually affected a client review, and I’m worried people are starting to wonder if I can really handle the promotion. I hate saying that out loud, but that’s probably the biggest reason I felt like I should come in.
